passage:
Asif was eleven, on his mother's phone after homework. He had asked his friend Vinita, "Can I borrow your cricket cards for Saturday?" The reply came in a second: "ok".
Only two letters, no smiley, no "sure!" Asif stared at it. Vinita was angry about the torn card last week, he thought. His stomach felt heavy. He typed "sorry" and deleted it.
"What's wrong?" asked Amma, folding clothes nearby.
"Vinita said ok. Just ok."
"Ask her, then."
Asif typed, "Are you angry with me?" A minute later: "no silly!! I was doing dance steps, thumbs only 😄"
Asif laughed and let out a long breath.

qa.q: What did Vinita write in reply to the request about cricket cards?
Why did Asif's stomach feel heavy after reading Vinita's reply?
qa.a: Asif was worried that Vinita was angry about the torn card. The short "ok" had no smiley, so Asif read it through that fear.

qa.q: What did Asif do that cleared up the worry?
qa.a: Asif asked Vinita straight out whether Vinita was angry. Vinita answered that the reply was short because of dance steps and thumbs only.

qa.q: Why might Vinita have written such a short reply?
qa.a: Vinita was busy doing dance steps and typing with thumbs only, so a quick "ok" was all that fit. It was not meant to show anger.

grounding: A child reads a short "ok" from a friend as anger, then checks and learns the friend was busy.

passage:
"Ganga, why are you angry with me?" Tarun stood by the school bus, backpack half open.
"I'm not!"
"You wrote 'k'. Only 'k'. You are my best friend and you always write 'okay okay okay!'"
Ganga blinked. "I was on the bus stairs. I was holding my bag with one hand. I only had space for one letter."
"But it looked cross."
"It looked cross because you read it in a cross voice," Ganga said, and giggled. "I'm happy. I got the last mango bar today."
Tarun let out a laugh. "Next time write two letters, okay?"
"Okay okay okay!" said Ganga, and held out half the bar.

qa.q: What single letter did Ganga send in the message?
What was Tarun feeling when Tarun asked Ganga why Ganga was angry?
qa.a: Tarun was worried and unsure, because Ganga usually wrote "okay okay okay!" and the lone "k" looked cross. Tarun needed to hear it out loud.

qa.q: What could Tarun try when a short message feels cold?
qa.a: Tarun could ask the friend directly, as Tarun did at the bus. Asking in person or by call lets the voice and face show how the friend really feels.

qa.q: How did Ganga see the message "k" when it was written?
qa.a: Ganga saw it as just a fast reply typed with one hand on the bus stairs. Ganga did not know the letter would look cross to Tarun.

grounding: A child reads a friend's short "k" as anger, and the friend explains it was just a rushed message.
